summary: Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Kenneth de Burgh Codrington studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College, Oxford. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (~1931-1948), University of London (~1948-1965), and University of Cincinnati.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Aichi Gakuin University (2000-2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (director in 2025).

Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who completed doctoral studies at Otani University. He has served as an emeritus professor at Hanazono University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Kenryu Tsuji was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kenryu Tsukinowa studied at Bukkyo University. He served as professor at Koyasan University (1926), Shuchiin University (1955), and Seizan Junior College, and became emeritus professor at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenshi Kusano specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from ~1971 to 1980 and served as a professor there around 2003.
A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kensur Yeshe Thupten held posts as a visiting Tibetan scholar at the University of Virginia in 1982 and at Middlebury College in 1982.

Kenta Suzuki works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held an associate professorship at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2013.

Kenyo Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968-2015) and held a visiting post at UC Berkeley in 1987.
Keshub Chunder Sen was a religious studies and Indology figure who studied at Hindu School, Presidency University (~1853-1858), and the University of Calcutta, and founded the Brahmo Samaj of India.

Kevin A. Vose works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, and his teachers included doctoral supervisors Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.
Kexin Zheng is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied as a PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Khakyab Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and the 1st Beru Khyentse Rinpoche.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000-2004). He served as a fellow at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2004) and founded the Shan State Buddhist University in 2014.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Palyul Choktrul Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Akyong Tokden Lodrö Gyatso.
Khantipālo studied under Sangharakshita (~1960-1965), Dhardo Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and taught Ayya Khema.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Pema Wangchok Gyelpo and Khakyab Dorje.
